metadata.title: Continuous Grassmannian Brascamp--Lieb inequalities and their equality cases
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we establish the forward and reverse geometric Brascamp--Lieb inequalities for isotropic measures on a Grassmann manifold, and characterize their equality conditions. The proofs use transportation and the Grassmannian Ball--Barthe inequality of Li, Xi, and Zhang. The functions form a jointly continuous family whose fiber integrals are positive and continuous. The equality conditions are described by an orthogonal decomposition determined by the supporting projections. On the common eigenspaces, the forward inequality permits arbitrary independent factors, whereas the reverse inequality requires log-concavity for factors shared by a nontrivial parameter distribution. On the orthogonal complement, the extremizers have Gaussian factors. Their centers are compatible projections in the forward inequality and may vary continuously between fibers in the reverse inequality. Gaussian convolution preserves extremizers, and the original factors are recovered at a fixed positive time using characteristic functions. As applications, we obtain Gaussian rigidity results and volume bounds for bodies defined by projection integrals and barycentric infima. These bounds recover the reverse isoperimetric inequalities of Li, Xi, and Zhang for bodies associated with Grassmannian cosine transforms, together with their equality conditions away from the endpoint cases. We also establish a forward extension under weaker mass assumptions and give a mass-escape example for the reverse inequality.
